# Synthetic e-commerce service architecture

This document describes only the isolated Phase 4 e-commerce simulation. It contains no real customer, payment, or production-system information.

## Request flow

```text
Operator load generator
        |
        v
API Gateway simulation
        |
        v
Checkout Service -------> Database Pool Simulator
        |
        +-----------------> Order Service (only after the database step succeeds)
```

The API Gateway simulation is the only component exposed on the host, bound to loopback. It provides health, synthetic load, state inspection, failure-injection, rollback, and report endpoints. Its Docker network is internal.

The Checkout Service receives synthetic checkout requests. It first asks the Database Pool Simulator to acquire a simulated connection and complete an in-memory query. When that step succeeds, it sends an in-memory order request to the Order Service. If database acquisition times out, checkout returns a synthetic error and does not create an order.

The Order Service allocates synthetic order identifiers in process memory. The Database Pool Simulator is not a database server and stores no business records; it models a configurable connection limit and request contention only. `DB_POOL_SIZE=50` is the healthy demo configuration. The controlled failure scenario changes this setting to `10` and the guarded rollback restores it to `50`.

No service calls a payment processor, external order platform, or production database.
